src: Cedar Rapids Gazette, 11 Oct 1897, p. 1 (Williamsburg dispatch; Newspapers.com 551618500)
Muscatine Journal, 15 Oct 1897, p. 6, 'Miser Fatally Beaten' (Newspapers.com 542372617)
tw-ia-conroy-olson-tomato-cans-1898.t: The 1897 wire says he banked $12,000 after the torture; treat the remaining caches as belief.

set.st: Ole Olson, an early settler who lived alone north of Conroy, distrusted banks and kept most of his money in tomato cans hidden in holes in the ground. About 1894 three masked men bound and tortured him until he gave up one hiding place; after that, a Williamsburg dispatch said, he deposited over $12,000 in the banks. He was reckoned worth $30,000 and lived in a hovel in a field on one of his farms, his two sons farming nearby. On the night of Friday 8 Oct 1897 he was struck behind the ear and died on the 10th; there was no clue, and the murder was never solved. The 1904 account's 'six years ago' was loose. In late May 1904 two men drove in at night and were seen digging; four fresh holes were found around a tree near the house. Nothing is reported found. Pin is Conroy, not the farm.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: the 1897 murder and the 1904 night dig are period-reported, but the 1897 dispatch says Olson banked over $12,000 after the torture, so the cans in the ground are the diggers' belief, not the record's; no recovery reported.
